title: Mechanisms of granulocyte homeostasis
text:
The proposed work exploits single-cell analytics to characterize the molecular signature of the homeostatic
state of hematopoiesis that sustains health and wellness. Specifically, it will generate gene regulatory networks
for hematopoietic progenitors, which integrate the activity of transcription factors (TFs), enhancers and
chromatin to reveal a blueprint underlying those patterns, and illustrating the drivers of developmental cell fate
decisions.

title: Deciphering inv3/t(3;3) Myeloid Leukemia Vulnerabilities via Proteogenomics and N-terminal Proteomics
text:
Patients suffering from inv3/(3;3) myeloid leukemias experience low 5-year survival rates (<5%) as a result of a
lack of targeted therapies and poor response to standard treatment regimens such as bone marrow transplant
in combination with chemotherapy. This work will utilize innovative proteogenomic approaches to identify
actionable targets for pharmacological studies and provide key mechanistic insights into the historically
“undruggable” inv3/(t3;3) myeloid leukemia cancer cell biology. As a result of this work, I anticipate an addition
to research on inv3/t(3;3) myeloid leukemias, with a long term impact of improving overall quality of and length
of life for patients.

title: Targeting Glutamine Uptake via ASCT2 Inhibition in MYCN-amplified Neuroblastomas
text: Neuroblastoma (NB) is the most common extracranial solid tumor in children. MYCN-amplification is present in ~25% of NBs and nearly half of all high-risk NBs. N-MYC is a proto-oncogene that drives cancer cell growth, angiogenesis, and metabolism. Aberrant glutamine metabolism is a hallmark of MYC-driven cancers. N-MYC enhances expression of the glutamine transporter, ASCT2. ASCT2 has been shown to be critical for MYCN-amplified NB cell survival in vitro and in subcutaneous xenograft formation in vivo. Our central hypothesis is that aberrant glutamine uptake via ASCT2 is critical for MYCN-amplified NB primary tumor growth and metastasis. We will define the critical role of ASCT2 in NB utilizing CRISPR-Cas9 knockout and V-9302, a small molecule ASCT2 inhibitor, in 3-D organoid and patient-derived orthotopic xenograft (PDOX) models of MYCN-amplified NB. Stable-isotope resolved metabolomics will be used to define aberrant metabolic pathways activated to sustain NB survival in the presence of ASCT2 blockade. We will also seek to define metabolic vulnerabilities uncovered by ASCT2 inhibition utilizing an unbiased CRISPR-Cas9 lineage dropout screen to assess for dual synthetic lethality in MYCN-amplified NB cells.

title: VCP in ASPSCR1::TFE3-driven oncogenic transcription reprogramming
text:
Alveolar soft part sarcoma is a deadly cancer that is caused by a mutation resulting in the aberrant fusion of
two genes, ASPSCR1 and TFE3. Alterations in gene expression caused by the fusion protein depend on
interactions with a protein unfolding machine known as VCP. This study aims to define the role of VCP in
driving the altered gene expression associated with the ASPSCR1-TFE3 fusion protein.

title: Investigating reciprocal interactions between circuit and synaptic function
text:
The pattern in which neurons are interconnected is a powerful determinant of how the brain functions, and
experience-dependent changes in these connection patterns likely underlie learning and memory. However,
the fundamental rules that link circuit connectomes to information processing are unknown, and it is unclear
how activity during experience specifically modifies the connectivity within a neural network to allow memories
to be later retrieved or how this process is pathologically altered in human neurological disorders. This
research will identify the relationship between connection patterns at the cellular level and network function at
the circuit level to reveal fundamental principles that govern information processing, memory formation, and
retrieval.

title: Interpretable deep learning models for translational medicine Renewal
text:
Colorectal cancer (CRC) is the 3rd most common cancer and the 2nd leading cause of cancer
death. After surgery, patients receive chemotherapy, including a drug called oxaliplatin, to
prevent the recurrence of cancer. Oxaliplatin benefits less than 10% of patients, but it causes
disabling neurotoxicity (nerve damage) in over 90% of patients. This project aims to develop an
artificial intelligence model to predict which patient would benefit from oxaliplatin so that
clinicians can choose different regimens to maximize efficacy and minimize unnecessary side
effects.

title: Training Program in Lung Biology and Pathobiology
text:
This training grant application seeks support for 5 predoctoral and 3 postdoctoral trainees. These individuals will
undergo training provided by well-positioned multi-disciplinary faculty in the rapidly evolving and increasingly
competitive field of lung biology and pathobiology. The 5 thematic areas of research training include (1) Lung
Vascular Homeostasis, Pathobiology, and Regeneration; (2) Cellular, Humoral, and Mechanical Bases of Lung
Injury and Repair; (3) Microbiome and Metabolism in Lung Biology and Pathobiology; (4) Lung Genomics and
Data Science in Inflamed and Regenerated Vessels, and (5) Therapeutics Targeting Lung Vessel Regeneration.
The goal is to cultivate highly qualified groups of young scientists capable of developing their careers in academic
research and alternative pathways.

title: CRISPR Generated Genomic Templates to Evaluate Epileptogenesis
text:
The health burdens of pediatric epilepsies are some of the most intractable. A better
understanding of Developmental and Epileptic Encephalopathy (DEE)—a severe pediatric
epileptic illness is expected to improve therapies and remediation. At its most optimistic, a better
understanding might lead to a better targeted anti-epileptic drug -which would be a profound
public health improvement.

title: Molecular Mechanism of an Exporter-like ABC Importer YbtPQ
text:
The proposed research is relevant to public health because it seeks to improve our understanding of the
siderophore-mediated metal uptake process in uropathogenic E. coil, the leading cause of urinary tract infections.
It will provide a concrete knowledge foundation for developing drugs to battle bacterial infections, which is
relevant to the NIH’s mission.

title: X-ray dark-field imaging of carotid hemodynamics enhanced by anisotropic IONP
text:
_________________________________________________________________________________
Relevance to Public Health h
The morbidity/mortality of cerebrovascular diseases (CVD) ranks 5th in the major causes of death and
disability in the US, necessitating more investment in basic and clinical research to address the unmet
needs in its prevention, diagnosis, prognosis, and therapeutic intervention. As a minimum invasive
procedure, digital subtraction angiography (DSA) is the gold-standard for CVD diagnosis and
therapeutic intervention, but it can only provide subjective and semiquantitative time-density profile-
based information on blood flow, in addition to the anatomic information, such as stenosis or
malformation. In this study, we explore the feasibility of X-ray dark-field imaging with anisotropic iron
dioxide nanorods as the contrast agent for visualization of complex flow patterns (zones) that may
support quantitative characterization of hemodynamic features, such as wall shear (WS) stress and WS
oscillation, in the carotid arteries for clinical management of CVD via prevention, diagnosis, therapeutic
intervention, and efficacy assessment.

title: Macrophage spatial heterogeneity in regulating hematopoietic aging
text:
Chronic inflammation in aging leads to blood stem cell expansion in the bone marrow. These cells have defective
regenerative potential, which leads to increased risks of infection, anemia, and blood malignancies. We observed
that blood stem cells are protected from systemic inflammation in a subset of bone marrow cavities and aim to
elucidate the underlying cellular-molecular mechanisms. The goal is to identify targetable therapeutic candidates
to counteract undesired division of blood stem cells in hematopoietic aging.

title: Mechanisms linking the frail sarcomere to noncompaction cardiomyopathy
text:
Genetic changes in the single gene, MYH7, which encodes the major motor protein in the heart, cause a
variety of human heart diseases, called cardiomyopathies. Up to 1/250 individuals carries a genetic change
in this gene. Through this work, we will detail why specific genetic defects cause a specific type of
developmental heart disease which manifest as cardiomyopathies, and this information will help identify and reduce disease risk

title: Transition Metal Homeostasis and Reactive Sulfur Chemistry in Bacterial Pathogens
text:
Acinetobacter baumannii and Streptococcus pneumoniae, among others, are significant threats to global human
health, particularly as these organisms acquire multidrug resistance. In this proposal, we outline a broad-based
strategy to significantly enhance our understanding of two regulatory processes linked to the survival of these
organisms in the infected host. How bacterial cells adapt to host-mediated changes in the availability of essential
transition metal nutrients and leverage the host dietary antioxidant ergothioneine, hydrogen sulfide biogenesis
and signaling are the focus of these studies, potentially leading to the identification of new targets for the
development of novel antimicrobial therapies.

title: Pragmatic Trial of Remote tDCS and Somatosensory Training for Phantom Limb Pain with Machine Learning to Predict Treatment Response
text:
Chronic Phantom Limb Pain (PLP) is recognized as very difficult to treat as it is often resistant to classical
pharmacological and surgical treatment approaches. Our previous R01 and research studies have shown
significant and robust results to support a combined therapy with tDCS and somatosensory training. In this study
we propose to test the real-world effects of home-based tDCS combined with a somatosensory training in a
pragmatic trial design and a machine-learning analysis to find the best predictors of response.

title: WashU-VAI Somatic Mosaicism across Human Tissues (SMaHT) Program Genome Characterization Center
text:
The WashU-VAI Somatic Mosaicism across Human Tissues (SMaHT) Program Genome Characterization
Center (SMaHT-GCC) will identify and characterize multiple types of human somatic variation (SNVs, structural
variants, and mobile DNA elements) from multiple tissues from multiple donors using high-throughput genomic
sequencing including long-read sequencing and single cell sequencing, provide these data to the SMaHT Data
Analysis Center, and ultimately contribute to the construction of the SMaHT Variant Catalog.

title: DNA-optical barcoding technology for spatiotemporal single-cell analysis
text:
This application will lead to commercialization of a new technology with immediate benefits for life science
research by addressing the current challenge of obtaining comprehensive information from individual cells.
This advancement will accelerate biological discoveries in areas such as cancer, immunology, and stem
cell biology.

title: Investigation of how RNA-directed feedback loops coordinate wound healing and regeneration
text:
Numerous disease states ranging from excessive migration in pulmonary fibrosis, incomplete wound
repair in uncontrolled diabetes, and the metastatic spread of aggressive tumors have altered cell
migration. Several developmental pathways are re-expressed during injury under normal and
diseased conditions. The goal of my lab is to further our understanding of wound-healing during
normal compared to disease states using development as a road map.

title: Unveiling mechanisms of RNA editing dysregulation
text:
This proposal will uncover how viruses manipulate ADARs to subvert host defenses, reveal conserved viral
strategies for regulating RNA editing, and define how inosine edits impact immune activation. This work will
reveal molecular principles of host-virus conflict to improve treatments for autoimmune diseases, viral infections,
and RNA-based therapeutics.

title: Home-based actigraphy to predict disability progression and enhance clinical trials in multiple sclerosis
text:
Wearable accelerometers provide an inexpensive, non-invasive means of measuring patterns of activity, sleep,
and circadian rhythm in a real-world setting, and the data emerging from our ongoing work show that in a
population of individuals with multiple sclerosis (MS), alterations in the metrics, including related to sleep, are
associated with subsequent evidence of atrophy of the brain, itself a precursor to worsening of disability. New
analytical advances applied to other neurologic diseases demonstrate that nuanced alterations in walking and
arm movements captured by accelerometers are associated with greater burden of symptoms. In our ongoing,
prospective cohort of people with MS, we propose to further characterize components of sleep, arm, and gait
measures and how they relate, alone or in combination with imaging measures of tissue loss and chronic
inflammation in the central nervous system, to disability progression, work that will ultimately help advance
clinical trials and thus outcomes for people with MS who are experiencing, or are at risk of, worsening function.

title: Predicting fatal and non-fatal overdose in Los Angeles County with Rapid Overdose Surveillance Dashboard to target street-based addiction treatment and harm reduction services
text:
Targeted overdose prevention requires timely, localized data to inform healthcare policy and to effectively direct
resources and interventions. However, such information is often unavailable, resulting in responses that are
often, “after the fact.” In this proposal, we plan to partner with five local government agencies to develop data-
driven tools and processes to rapidly acquire and analyze information to identify overdose hotspots and “now-
cast” overdose metrics in near-real-time.
